summary: Enable Status Page comms templates + workflow for Dedicated throughput SLO breach notifications
description:
Background
- We are rolling out Dedicated throughput SLOs + tiered commitments. Support/CS needs a consistent, pre-approved external communication workflow for SLO breaches (or potential breaches) that can be executed quickly by oncall.
- Current gap: no standardized Status Page templates for Dedicated throughput SLO degradation (customer-facing wording, update cadence, what we can/can’t promise, and when to mention credits/remedies).

Problem
- During recent throughput investigations (see SUP-18422, SUP-18510) comms were ad-hoc and inconsistent across Support, CS, and SRE.
- Customers (esp. enterprise Dedicated) are asking for “in writing” acknowledgement of SLO misses and clear timelines/updates; we need a repeatable workflow aligned with SRE incident policy.

Request
1) Create Status Page incident templates specific to Dedicated throughput SLO breach communications:
   - Initial notice (Investigating)
   - Identified + mitigation in progress
   - Monitoring
   - Resolved
   - Post-incident summary (optional, within 2–5 business days)
2) Define operational workflow:
   - When to open a Status Page event vs. keep comms 1:1 (account-specific)
   - Who owns posting (Support oncall vs. SRE oncall) and approval path
   - Update cadence targets (e.g., every 60 min while active, then at resolution)
   - Links/fields to include (customer-facing dashboard references, if any)
3) Add “do not say” guidance:
   - Don’t share exact committed tokens/sec floors, internal headroom numbers, or affected customer list unless approved.
   - Don’t attribute root cause prematurely (e.g., “GPU shortage”) without SRE confirmation.
   - Avoid implying SLA remedies/credits unless Finance/CS policy is triggered.

Proposed scope for templates
- Dedicated Throughput Degradation (Tier-wide / Regional) template
- Dedicated Throughput Degradation (Single-customer deployment) template (generally avoid Status Page unless multiple customers impacted; prefer direct comms, but template should exist)

Acceptance criteria
- Templates added to Status Page tool (component: “Dedicated Inference (Throughput)”) with pre-filled language + placeholders.
- Workflow documented in Support runbook (link added to Dedicated throughput SLO escalation playbook).
- Approval list explicitly named: Support oncall owner, SRE oncall, CS lead on duty, and escalation to Commercial Counsel if remedy language is included.
- Training note posted in #support and #customer-success with where-to-find templates and when-to-use guidance.

Notes
- This ticket is about comms + operational workflow only (not SLO definition changes).
- Target date: before broader Dedicated tier enablement rollout.
comments:
2025-02-19 10:22 Dev Patel (reporter)
Created after reviewing recent Dedicated throughput cases where we lacked a consistent external comms pattern. Need something lightweight but enforceable before more accounts get tiered SLO language.

2025-02-20 14:05 Rachel Kim
+1. For enterprise accounts, CS ends up drafting emails from scratch during an incident. Even if we don’t post publicly on Status Page for single-account events, having approved language and cadence guidance will reduce time-to-first-update and de-risk legal wording.

2025-02-21 09:48 Rafael Mendes
From SRE side: we’re fine with a Status Page template as long as we keep it generic and don’t publish per-customer metrics. Recommend: only post if (a) multiple Dedicated customers in a region, (b) sustained SLO burn-rate alert indicates likely breach, or (c) SRE declares customer-impacting incident. Otherwise use the 1:1 template.

2025-02-24 16:11 Kira Thompson (assignee)
Drafted template set v1 and shared in #support-ops for review. Open questions:
- Do we name specific regions in the public post (e.g., us-east) or keep it broader?
- Do we mention “throughput below expected” vs “increased queueing / reduced capacity” wording?
- Who is the final approver if we include credit/remedy language placeholder?

2025-02-25 11:36 Laura Bennett
For remedy language: keep as “Customer Success will follow up regarding account-specific remedies where applicable.” Do not mention credit % or formulas in Status Page posts. Any compensation details must be handled 1:1 by CS per policy.

2025-02-26 13:02 Sean Gallagher
Suggested aligning triggers with SLO semantics:
- Status Page Investigating when we have a confirmed platform-side capacity/throughput impairment affecting more than one Dedicated deployment OR a regional pool saturation event.
- Use ‘potential SLO impact’ phrasing until breach confirmed by the evaluator window.
- Add a line that measurement excludes customer-side throttling/misconfiguration to avoid self-inflicted reports being treated as platform incident.

2025-03-03 15:28 Dev Patel
Reviewed templates. Requested two variants:
(1) ‘Dedicated Throughput Degradation (multi-tenant pool / multiple customers)’ for Status Page
(2) ‘Dedicated Throughput Degradation (single customer)’ for direct email + ticket update
Also asked to include required internal links: dashboard panel and escalation runbook.

2025-03-05 10:17 Kira Thompson
Implemented changes and added workflow section. Final template text pasted into Status Page as saved templates under component group “Dedicated Inference (Throughput)”. Posted internal enablement note draft for review by Rachel + Rafael.

2025-03-07 09:04 Dev Patel
Enablement note posted to #support and #customer-success. Marking resolved. Follow-up: we should add a short checklist to oncall handoff doc (separate ticket if needed).
resolution: Saved Status Page templates created for Dedicated throughput incidents (multi-customer / regional). Direct-communication template created for single-customer Dedicated deployment throughput degradation. Operational workflow documented and linked from Dedicated throughput SLO escalation playbook; update cadence and approval guidance defined. Internal enablement note posted to #support and #customer-success.
status_page_templates_added: Dedicated Throughput Degradation (Single-customer) — Email/Ticket Update Pack
customer_facing_copy_snippets: Investigating: We are investigating reports of reduced throughput for Dedicated Inference in <REGION>. Some customers may experience reduced tokens/sec or increased queueing for eligible requests. We will provide an update within <CADENCE>.
Identified: We have identified an issue affecting Dedicated Inference throughput in <REGION> and are applying mitigations to restore expected performance. Next update in <CADENCE>.
Monitoring: Mitigations have been applied and we are monitoring recovery. Throughput is trending toward expected levels. We will update when fully resolved.

Resolved: This issue has been resolved and Dedicated Inference throughput has returned to expected levels. If you continue to observe issues, please contact Support with your deployment ID and timestamps.
do_not_say_guidance: Do not publish committed throughput floors, tokens/sec guarantees, internal headroom, or customer names on Status Page.
Do not state root cause until SRE confirms (avoid speculative wording like “GPU shortage” or “noisy neighbor”).
Do not mention specific credits/compensation percentages or eligibility criteria in public posts.
Do not imply that customer-side configuration errors are a platform incident; confirm platform-side impact first.
